rationale: Abstract Methods: "Cardiorespiratory parameters" were the outcomes (HR, RR, BP, VO2 max, PEFR, PCFR); Methods list no motivation questionnaire, only "Cognitive function was assessed using the Indonesian version"; motivation appears only in Introduction/Discussion as a rationale.

Methods, Neuropsychiatric Assessment: "Neuropsychiatric symptoms were assessed using the" Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI); only its apathy item/domain touches motivation (an apathy scale is out under I5); no exercise motivation instrument was used. Trial is randomized exergame vs active control, 16 sessions twice weekly.
doubt: I5: does the apathy domain of the NPI count as a motivation subscale? Read as an apathy scale (excluded by I5) not a motivation-for-exercise measure.

rationale: I5 instrument BREQ-3, Data Collection: "Behavioral Regulation in Exercise Questionnaire-3 (BREQ-3)"; I6 both arms, Findings: "motivation increased substantially in the VR group (M = 4.08, SD = 0.52)" vs control M = 3.15 (Table 1); I2/I3 Methods: "Participants were randomly assigned"; I4: "The intervention lasted eight structured sessions over two months"; published online 2025-04-01.
doubt: I1: the paper never names the VR game or says body movement is the game input ("VR exergame training"), so exergame status rests on the authors' label. I5/I6: a single composite "Exercise Motivation" score is reported on a 0-4 BREQ-3 scale yet means reach 4.08, and subscales are not reported; unclear how the composite was formed.

rationale: Header: "Perspective Article"; Abstract: "the authors aim to bridge key gaps in dual-task rehabilitation by providing clinical tools for application"; no trial, participants or motivation results.
